title: Ransomware recovery is now a client retention metric
content_md: The ransomware attack is over. Your team has restored the client’s data, brought systems back online and put business operations back on track. From a technical standpoint, the recovery was a success. But the client still has questions. Why did updates go quiet for two days? What drove the recovery costs up? And where did the 31 hours of emergency labor on the invoice come from? Recovering from ransomware is only part of the job. Clients also need to know what happened, what recovery involved and what it cost them. When communication falls short or unexpected charges appear, even a technically successful recovery can leave clients questioning the value of their MSP relationship. The disruption may be behind them, but their doubts can carry into the next renewal conversation. Ransomware recovery can take days, even when teams have backups and a response plan in place. According to industry reports, only 16% of affected organizations fully recovered within a day . Over half (55%) recovered within a week. For businesses that depend on their systems to serve customers and generate revenue, every additional day of disruption carries a cost. The stakes extend to the MSP, too. Kaseya’s 2026 Cybersecurity Outlook report found that 12% of MSPs lost clients following security incidents , with ransomware, account takeover and business email compromise among the main reasons.
